overview.text: The Florida Cottonmouth is a venomous pit viper of Florida and southern Georgia, found in almost every kind of wetland there, even brackish water and islands.

identification.text: Its face markings are usually lighter and cleaner than the northern cottonmouth's, with two dark vertical lines on the snout.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The Florida peninsula, including many barrier islands and keys, and southern Georgia.

habitat.text: Swamps, edges of cypress ponds and wooded water margins - but it is not entirely tied to water.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to 1 to 15 live young, mostly in summer; females usually breed every other year. Females can sometimes reproduce without a male.

recognise.text: Thick, dark pit viper near water.
Two dark vertical lines on the snout.
